Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Jordan Lee, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV Inc.'s Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Alex Rivera, CFO; Mike Hargrove, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Priya Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q3, we are proud of the significant strides Apex EV has made across all facets of our business. We've delivered robust total revenue growth, accelerated our software and services revenue streams, expanded factory capacities with enhanced operational efficiencies, advanced our supply chain resilience against raw material volatility and disruptions, sharpened our strategic priorities for scalable profitability, and provided clear revenue and margin guidance that underscores our momentum. The market reception to our flagship Apex S sedan and Apex X SUV has been overwhelmingly positive, with associated delivery ramps and autonomy feature adoption far exceeding our initial estimates, driving premium mix shifts and recurring revenue uplift.

These achievements position us strongly in a competitive EV landscape, where we're outpacing peers through vertical integration and tech leadership. Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. Our revenue for Q3 reached $2.85 billion, marking an exceptional 52% increase compared to the same period last year. This underscores the accelerating momentum in our EV ecosystem, surpassing our internal guidance midpoint by 8% and marking our 11th consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year revenue expansion. On a trailing twelve-month basis, revenue now stands at $9.2 billion, positioning us as one of the fastest-scaling pure-play EV OEMs globally.

Breaking this down, vehicle revenue accounted for 82% of total at $2.34 billion, surging 61% year-over-year, fueled by record deliveries of 162,000 units—up 68% from 96,500 last year. Average selling price held steady at $112,000 per vehicle, reflecting a premium mix toward higher-margin models like the Apex S sedan, which ramped to 45% of mix with 73,000 units, enabled by our 4680 cell architecture for 15% better energy density and 420-mile EPA range. The Apex X SUV hit 32% mix at 52,000 units, boosted by over-the-air Level 3 autonomy updates, while commercial vans added 37,000 units, capturing 12% U.S. last-mile share amid fleet electrification mandates.

Energy generation and storage revenue grew to $380 million, or 13% of total, up 38% year-over-year, including Powerwall 3 home batteries up 45% to 120,000 installations and Megapack deployments, highlighted by a 500 MWh contract with Southern California Edison using our LFP-NMC hybrid cathodes for 20% higher cycle life.

Services and other revenue reached $130 million, up 42%, driven by Supercharge network expansion to 4,200 stalls at 95% uptime and Apex Autonomy subscriptions at 28% attach rate.

Regionally, North America contributed 45% at $1.28 billion, up 67%, supercharged by IRA credits and Gigafactory Texas at 250,000 annual capacity for 18% U.S. EV share in the $50K+ segment. China delivered 28% or $800 million, up 45%, via Shanghai JV with CATL despite price wars, leveraging sodium-ion pilots for affordability. Europe was 20% at $570 million, up 39%, with Berlin plant output compliant with WLTP.

This growth stems from supply chain resilience derisking 85% of battery materials against lithium volatility, tech leadership like 800V architecture for 18-minute charges, and digital direct sales at 65% of volume plus Hertz's 50,000-unit order. Gross margins expanded 420 basis points to 24.8%, supporting adjusted EBITDA of $450 million.

A key highlight is our software and services revenue, which hit a record $1.45 billion in the quarter—though integrated across segments—up 52% year-over-year from $952 million, representing a sharp acceleration and industry-leading 82% gross margins, over three times vehicle hardware profitability. Subscriptions drove 65% at $943 million, up 61%, with Voltara Premium tier at $15/month bundling infotainment and AI range optimization, achieving 68% attachment and 92% renewal, ARPU at $285 annualized. Autonomous driving added 28% or $406 million, up 112%, with 450,000 activations and 1.2 billion fleet miles logged on our NVIDIA-powered supercomputer. Services like Charge Network rounded out at 7%, with RPO at $8.7 billion, 75% recognizing within 12 months.

Turning to outlook, for Q4 we expect $3.1-3.3 billion, 50-60% year-over-year growth, and full-year FY2024 at $10.8-11.2 billion, 110% growth, with 2025 ASPAC expansion targeting 650,000 deliveries. For Q4 specifically, $2.85-2.95 billion, 25-30% growth, anchored by 42,000-45,000 deliveries, ASP $62,000-64,000 with regulatory credits adding $180 million, non-vehicle $350 million. FY2025 raised to $12.5-13.5 billion, 45-60% growth, 210,000-230,000 deliveries.

Gross margins guide to 22-24% for Q4, 24-26% FY2025, from $31,000-32,000 COGS per vehicle via LFP shift to 60%, 4680 ramp, gigacasting savings of $800/vehicle, 92% utilization. ASP steady at $45,000 with 45% premium mix, volume leverage from 375,000 deliveries. North America benefits from IRA passthrough, Europe from tariffs on China, China capped exposure.

Raw material costs and disruptions added $450 million to COGS, contracting margins 280 bps to 21.4%, with lithium up 22% YoY averaging $42,000/ton, nickel surges from Indonesian curbs, aluminum premiums at $550/ton. Supply disruptions delayed 12,000 deliveries, semis at 28-week leads, cell bottlenecks from graphite shortages and Red Sea shipping spikes to $12,000/FEU. Mitigated by LFP shift reducing nickel 60%, in-house NovaCell to 20 GWh, offtakes hedging 80% lithium, Redwood recycling at 95% yield.

Our $15 billion liquidity funds Giga Mexico, solid-state R&D. Operator, next we'll hear from Mike Hargrove on manufacturing.

Mike Hargrove:
Thank you, Alex. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet surging demand. We've deployed $2.8 billion in CapEx year-to-date, 65% to expansions like Reno Gigafactory Phase 2 ramping to 120 GWh on 4680 dry electrode cells for 600,000 vehicles, Brandenburg to 400,000 units with EU-compliant packs, and India JV for 250,000 sub-$30K EVs using 9,000-ton Giga Presses cutting cycle times 60%.

Operational efficiencies via NovaVolt Lean 2.0 delivered 12% COGS reduction to $28,500/vehicle: AI predictive maintenance cut downtime 28% saving $145 million, 1,200 robots boosted OEE to 94%, digital twins shortened prototyping 56%, in-house cathodes dropped costs 22%, solar microgrids trimmed energy 15%. Factory-in-a-box de-risks ramps, localizing 75% minerals for 400 bps margin lift in 2025.

Following me, Dr. Priya Singh will update on innovations.

Dr. Priya Singh:
Thank you. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, autonomous driving systems, and vehicle connectivity. We're rolling out Gen 3 autonomy for Level 3 hands-free, with 99.8% disengagement-free miles from LiDAR-camera fusion and 1.2 billion real-world miles training neural nets. Battery innovations include LFP-sodium hybrids for 750-mile trucks, solid-state pilots at 800 Wh/kg for 10-minute charges via QuantumScape JV, and OTA Adaptive Energy Management boosting efficiency 8%. Our 800V architecture and AI manufacturing yield 25% higher throughput, with $450 million Q4 R&D for software-defined vehicles and end-to-end vertical integration.

After me, Raj Patel on supply chain.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. We have established a resilient network, improving on-time delivery to 92%. Semis delays idled lines 5 days, battery pricing spiked 8% from export bans and Red Sea routes, but diversification cut single-source dependency to 22%, TSMC Arizona for MCUs, Panasonic Reno at 50 GWh supplying 60%. AI forecasting at 88% accuracy, strategic inventory at 12 weeks semis, blockchain tracking. IRA localization de-risks 70% cathodes, Northvolt LFP in Europe, Mexico packs qualifying credits. Hedging 80% exposure forecasts <5% impact Q1'25, turning headwinds to tailwinds for 15-20% growth.

Next, Maria Gonzalez on sales.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you. Our sales team achieved remarkable success expanding reach, with strong demand across regions: North America 35% growth on IRA and fleets, Europe 50% via Berlin despite tariffs, China premium exports, emerging pilots. Digital direct at 65%, Hertz 50,000 order, 42% autonomy attach driving $2,500 lifetime value. We're pursuing APAC, LATAM opportunities for 40-50% FY25 growth.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Can you elaborate on the drivers behind the 52% revenue growth and how sustainable it is given macro headwinds?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question. Absolutely, the 52% growth was driven by 68% delivery increase to 162,000 units on premium mix, energy storage wins like the 500 MWh Edison deal, and services up 42% from Supercharge and autonomy subs at 28% attach. Sustainability comes from supply resilience shielding lithium volatility, 800V tech, and direct sales agility—our TTM $9.2 billion run-rate and Q4 guide to $3.1-3.3 billion show we're navigating softening demand and competition from Tesla, BYD effectively, on track for 110% FY24 growth.

Analyst 2:
Great, follow-up for Alex: On software revenue, what's the latest on attach rates and RPO recognition?

Alex Rivera:
Sure, software/services at $1.45 billion, 52% YoY, 82% margins—subscriptions 65% with 68% attach, 92% renewal, ARPU $285; autonomy 28% with 75% QoQ activations, 1.2 billion miles. RPO $8.7 billion, 75% in 12 months, SaaS-like stickiness with 94% cohort retention. Q3 guide $1.65-1.75 billion, FY $6.4-6.6 billion, scaling to $25 billion by 2027 with Robotaxi.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Mike, on factory expansions, any updates on timelines and CapEx returns?

Mike Hargrove:
Thanks. Reno Phase 2 to 120 GWh Q4'25 on 4680 dry electrode, Brandenburg 400K vehicles next month, India JV H2'25 for 250K with Giga Press. $2.8 billion YTD CapEx yielding 12% COGS drop via AI maintenance, robots at 94% OEE. Total capacity 1.8M vehicles/200 GWh by '26, ROIC >20%, 400 bps margin lift '25.

Analyst 4:
Priya, how does your autonomy stack compare to competitors, and battery roadmap?

Dr. Priya Singh:
Our Gen 3 stack hits Level 3 beta Q4 with 99.8% disengagement-free, 1.5M-pixel LiDAR edge over FSD Supervised, trained on 1.2B miles vs. Waymo geofenced. Batteries: Q1 Apex T LFP-sodium 750 miles, mid-'25 solid-state 800 Wh/kg 10-min charge, OTA efficiency +8%, $450M R&D fueling moat.

Analyst 5:
Raj, details on raw material impacts and supply mitigations this quarter?

Raj Patel:
Raw materials inflated COGS $1,850/vehicle 6.2%: lithium $42K/ton +22% YoY, nickel peaks, aluminum $550/ton; disruptions delayed 12K units, semis 28 weeks, Red Sea +40% freight. Mitigated by LFP 30% mix -60% nickel, 80% hedges, in-house 20 GWh, recycling 95% yield—Q4 lithium $35-45K, cells $105/kWh, margins to 23-25%.

Analyst 6:
Maria, sales outlook by region amid pricing pressures?

Maria Gonzalez:
Demand strong: NA 65% mix +35% IRA fleets, Europe +50% tariffs shield, China premium ASP RMB450K, emerging 5% growing. 42% sub attach $2,500 LTV, digital 65%, Hertz win—FY25 850-900K deliveries, 40-50% growth.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 7:
For Elena, strategic priorities for Q4/FY25?

Elena Vasquez:
Q4: 180K deliveries +25% seq, Apex X Gen3 autonomy beta, Texas 2 GWh. FY25: 850-900K, Apex T launch Q1, solid-state mid-year, 25-27% margins, NA 12% share, Europe 150K, supply 15% COGS cut. $8.2B cash, EBITDA 18%, flawless execution for mobility future.

Analyst 8:
Alex, gross margin assumptions and risks?

Alex Rivera:
FY25 24-26%: COGS $31-32K via LFP $45/kWh, 4680 16% lower, gigacast $800 save, 92% util, $45K ASP 45% premium. NA IRA +15% ASP, Europe +300 bps. Risks: lithium double +$2K/veh, supply delays; upside credits $250/unit, Mexico ramp +200 bps—FCF positive H2'25.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Inc. Q3 FY2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
